method: Read RULES.md and TAXONOMY.md; atomscan slow-mode JSON and cleave facts on both originals; CIL disassembly via dnfile/dncil; native control-flow and call tracing with Rizin/Capstone; isolated Unicorn emulation of pure decoding functions with allocation/crypto shims. No sample process, injected payload, or Windows API was executed.

samples.identification: ieo Windows PDF reader preview installer, 0.1.2-preview, Sentio Studio (self-declared publisher)
execution_trace: CIL entry point IeoPreviewInstaller.Main, RVA 0x2b44: requires explicit install/update consent except a GUID-scoped QA mode; installs under LocalApplicationData/Programs/ieo-preview.

Resources Payload and Manifest are an embedded ZIP and JSON manifest. SHA-256 of the ZIP and the size/hash of every one of 226 manifest entries match. Child() rejects traversal and drive-qualified paths and constrains extraction beneath its install directory; extraction checks duplicate entries and size limits.

Creates desktop/Start Menu shortcuts and the per-user Uninstall entry; keeps previous releases and reading data for rollback. Run-key update occurs only when an existing value points inside this installation and has the expected hidden-start suffix. Uninstall removes only its own startup setting/shortcuts and preserves the library.

Embedded ieo-native.exe is a .NET WinForms/WebView2 PDF reader. Traced its resource handler, bridge message dispatcher, startup settings, OAuth methods, Vault, and QA IPC. The ieo.example origin serves local bundled assets; network forwarding is constrained to Google API endpoints.

Google OAuth authorization code flow uses browser consent, loopback callback, state checking and PKCE for drive.file and drive.appdata. Vault.Write/Read use CurrentUser DPAPI for its own refresh authorization. Local PDFs, IndexedDB/history, PDF.js and user-initiated Drive synchronization match the advertised reader purpose.

QA named-pipe commands are enabled by explicit QA arguments, use a per-profile pipe and a current-user ACL, and expose diagnostics/lifecycle operations. No general remote-command interface or arbitrary downloaded payload execution was found.
provenance_and_dependencies: Outer installer and native reader are unsigned. Unsigned does not establish malicious intent; all source behavior was examined independently.

Fetched https://ieo-reader.pages.dev/ with forager. The site advertises this exact preview download and describes local PDFs and optional Google Drive history. Fetched its download with the requested SHA-256; it is byte-identical to the sample.

Fetched Microsoft.Web.WebView2 1.0.3967.48 from the official NuGet flat container. Core.dll, WinForms.dll and x64 WebView2Loader.dll all match the official package byte-for-byte. Authenticode content digests match; local full-chain verification lacks the issuing CA, so no trusted-chain claim is made.

Fetched the referenced Google api.js. Fetching Google Identity Services client returned HTTP 403. OAuth token/authorization URLs and Google service paths were traced as protocol endpoints, not treated as executable payload dependencies. XML namespaces, example URLs and React error-documentation URLs are library constants, not demonstrated callbacks.
samples.source_label_explanation: The collection reason is not provided. The minority antivirus results are generic ML/static labels; an unsigned managed installer with a compressed embedded archive and Run-key/COM/file-writing APIs is a plausible source of those alerts. No hostile loader, credential theft, unrelated endpoint or abusive configuration was found. Public distribution alone was not used to decide the verdict.
samples.missing_context: No deployment history or operator context is available. This is a sighted-quarantine BENIGN assessment of the reviewed bytes, not an authoritative benign training label.
samples.trait_decision: Retained all 82 original findings. They accurately record resource entropy, hashing, archive extraction, registry access and shortcut/file operations. No hostile or suspicious findings fired on the installer or the extracted reader bundle.
samples.marker_contents: ieo PDF preview: verified reader installer; all 82 traits retained

samples.identification: Trojanized Zapret Discord/YouTube 1.10.2 bundle carrying an obfuscated Go loader and Salat stealer/RAT
packaging: Fetched the original versioned release from Flowseal GitHub with forager. Official archive SHA-256: d9a57ab8254f1f8daa1c382736d7cd6ae60e5dbe128138844c3cf04648228330. Compared every member: 49 unchanged files, changed general.bat and service.bat, and added DiscordFix.exe.

The replacement launchers are 146-byte matching-basename launch stubs; the archive does not supply general.exe or service.exe. Do not claim these stubs launch DiscordFix.exe. The added executable is a separate lure/loader.

DiscordFix.exe SHA-256 424ab6ca20b47eeffe34c1f1ec3212f1db44aa022f5d55cc46def671b4d79300; its version metadata claims pnlhost.exe, Platform Services background service and Northwind Technologies. It is unsigned. These claims conflict with its wrapper role; attribution does not rely on the filename.

Cygwin, winws, WinDivert DLL and signed WinDivert driver match official members. The WinDivert driver Authenticode content digest also matches. Packet interception/reinjection and service capabilities are retained as accurate dual-use findings. Upstream third-party WinDivert/rootkit inventory labels are already notable, with config reasons explaining that the driver identity does not prove a rootkit.
loader_execution_trace: Recovered Go pclntab at file offset 0x50ca0 and mapped obfuscated functions to source files/lines. The application source appears as a generated Go file; stdlib/runtime names are also replaced.

Application main VA 0x4b7300 gates progress through multiple checks: NtQueryInformationProcess debugging classes, VM-agent paths with os.Stat, display/processor virtualization indicators, username/hostname heuristics, GetLastInputInfo, cursor movement and performance timing. False/suspicious results call os.Exit before payload decoding.

Global byte slices contain an XOR key byte followed by encoded strings. Recovered NtCreateSection, NtMapViewOfSection, NtProtectVirtualMemory, QueueUserAPC, ResumeThread; VM guest paths include VirtualBox, VMware and Qemu. No ciphertext or custom program identifier is required by the new detections.

Resource loader VA 0x4aa600 reads RCDATA 1. VA 0x4b1b40 reconstructs 3594331 bytes from a 6043249-byte stream of payload chunks interleaved with junk. VA 0x4b2200 applies the encoded segment permutation.

Main derives a 32-byte key with PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256, 100000 iterations, then VA 0x4b6220/0x4b65c0 apply a custom ARX stream transform. VA 0x4aafc0 inflates the result as raw DEFLATE. Pure-function emulation recovered a complete UPX PE; UPX decompression recovered the larger Go payload.

VA 0x4ab480 resolves native section APIs and QueueUserAPC/ResumeThread, selects a Windows System32 image, prepares a suspended child, maps the decrypted stage through a section, queues execution and resumes the thread. Fallback VA 0x4b0d40 writes a temporary executable and invokes os/exec.Command/Start. VA 0x4b5ee0 schedules removal with MoveFileExW. Static call paths establish attempted execution; runtime success was not claimed.

behavior_evidence: Salat main at VA 0x8d5410 calls runKeylogger, initializes control endpoints and polls through rq/changeEndpoint. Its code includes task dispatch and SOCKS relay functions.

getChromeLogins VA 0x8f2dc0 opens a SQLite browser store, calls database/sql.QueryContext with SELECT origin_url, action_url, username_value, password_value, date_created FROM logins at 0x8f2f64/0x8f2f8e, then calls DecryptChrome at 0x8f3279. This is credential extraction, not a string-only attribution.
runKeylogger VA 0x8d1e30 installs event/hook handling and stages recording; its screenshot path calls getScreen and rq. Dedicated salat/screenshot.Capture routines use Windows screen-capture APIs.

Recovered task/browser/wallet/messaging collection routines and native Salat identity match the execution paths. Existing hostile traits fire for Chromium credential theft, wallet/session harvesting, keylogger/screenshot collection and remote task/SOCKS behavior; CAPE and Elastic independently identify the extracted stage as Salat.
decoded_payload.limits: Final operator endpoint selection and live C2 reachability were not resolved or exercised; neither is required to establish theft and unauthorized payload execution.
decoded_payload.classifier: HOSTILE: score 0.990, fp-level L25, confirmed by live tiny render.

samples.verdict_reason: The added concealed loader performs analysis gating and activates an embedded credential-stealing remote-access payload. That behavior is unrelated to DPI circumvention; the official-member comparison independently proves altered packaging. Deployment context is absent, but it is unnecessary to invent one for this malicious bundle.
samples.coverage_gap: The outer loader receives two distinct suspicious findings for concealed injection APIs and the VM guest artifact list. Neither matcher claims execution of its referenced operations. The recovered stage has multiple existing hostile behaviors; the current scanner cannot automatically perform this custom multi-stage resource decoding, so those payload behaviors do not surface in the original archive scan. No hostile signature was fabricated from API co-occurrence just to satisfy a trait count.
samples.marker_contents: Zapret/Salat: concealed credential-stealing RAT; traits corrected

rule_changes.supported_claim: Five full native section-mapping/APC API names are XOR-concealed in an initialized non-executable PE data section. Suspicious concealment; does not assert an injection succeeded.
A nearby ordered list of full VirtualBox, VMware and Qemu guest artifact paths shares a nonzero XOR key in PE data. Suspicious concealed anti-VM target list; description does not claim an API call.

rule_changes.change: Narrow binary mtr recognition while retaining unchanged script recognition
rule_changes.unsupported_claim: Shuffled resource prose produced mtr 6e, mtr ia, and Mtr oi fragments, not a network diagnostic invocation. Binary commands now need a command boundary and a flag, address/domain-shaped target, or localhost. Script matcher scope and exclusions are retained; valid binary commands still fire under mtr-binary-command.

rule_changes.change: Narrow shell-dd-file-write to a direct sink or initial assignment/input redirection followed by a sink
rule_changes.unsupported_claim: Resource noise contained dd r 2tfdl muh > xa. Arbitrary positional words are not dd operands. Existing real disk-wipe fixtures and generated command carriers retain detection, including of= and direct redirection forms. Consumer shell-file-write-command and downstream file-write aggregation were audited. Input redirection and output redirection adjacent to dd are explicitly retained by positive controls.

--hostlist in Zapret configures a traffic filter; it is neither mass host exploitation nor evidence of a CVE. Matcher, platform/type scope, confidence and notable criticality are preserved; mass-cve and HTTP management-scan consumers reference the new ID. Removed inapplicable T1190 mapping from the atom.

rule_changes.change: Consolidate misplaced rar-fat-exe-member and rar-fat-bat-member into metadata/file/archive::rar-large-member-with-code-member
rule_changes.unsupported_claim: A large member plus an EXE/batch member is archive-table co-occurrence, not dropper behavior; the old exe description also did not bind the size to the executable. Size, executable-member and batch-member atoms remain individually visible. The neutral co-occurrence now surfaces without product-context suppressors. The destructive-batch consumer additionally requires the explicit batch atom and its prior relevant path/web-project exclusions. The old PE-only WinRAR suppressor could never apply to that RAR/batch consumer and was not copied. No severity reduction was used to hide a detection.

rule_changes.supported_claim: Former six-digit regex matched 200000..999999 bytes only, missing members above 1 MB. New regex covers every integer size >=200000; description states exact byte threshold. Existing exclusions are preserved. This is increased size coverage.

consumer_and_fixture_audit: No exact or ancestor consumers of the mtr atom/leaf were found. The source-script matcher is unchanged; binary false matches were demonstrated in the real loader resource, with positive binary command controls retained.

DD direct consumer is shell-file-write-command; downstream file-write aggregation still fires. Actual outside-batch fixtures testdata/impact-wipe/08-linux-hardcoded-sda.sh and testdata/version-drift/active-device.sh retain detection.

Host-file option exact consumers are mass-cve-exploitation-runner and bulk-http-management-path-scan; both pass focused controls after relocation. No additional exact/ancestor scanner consumers were found.

RAR pair exact consumer is rar-fat-batch-destructive-cleaner; a focused destructive archive still fires and ordinary large-member archives do not satisfy that objective. The broad dropper ancestor consumer windows-embedded-security-hosts-sinkhole no longer treats neutral archive pairing as a dropper. That PE/DLL hosts-poisoning rule does not fire in this batch.

All 63 archive analysis units (including batch-expansion layers) were compared by path before/after. Legitimate winws/WinDivert/Cygwin behaviors and identities are preserved. The original 49 unchanged upstream members were checked independently of the added loader.
classifier_disagreement: Atomscan v18.18/engine 2.13.0 still renders the malicious original archive BENIGN (score 0.9892427, calibrated level -1), despite increased suspicious coverage. DiscordFix.exe itself rises from 0.0005612274 to 0.0110257864 and is also below threshold. The manually recovered stage is recognized as hostile. This is a custom-decoder/classifier coverage gap; no inaccurate trait was restored or duplicated to raise its score. The model also warned that feature spec v18 predates extractor v19.
material_detection_losses: Only the two demonstrated junk-command matches are removed from the loader. Host-option evidence is relocated, and the two neutral RAR pairings are represented by one accurately described metadata relationship plus their still-visible constituent atoms. No supported hostile finding was lost in either original or their analyzed members.
validation_command: make validate (required final action after marker creation)
